title: Cost Ops Hypothesis Catalogue & Rollout Roadmap
creator: Priya Raman
description: Goal: Create a single source-of-truth hypothesis catalogue and corresponding rollout roadmap for cost-optimization experiments across batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization. The deliverable will let PMs and Eng run reproducible field experiments, capture regressions, and automate safe rollouts. Scope covers hypothesis templates, evaluation gating, experiment telemetry, canary/A-B rollout playbooks, and a prioritized backlog for Q2 execution. Out of scope: changing core scheduler kernels — that will be tracked separately with Eng runtime epic. This ticket focuses on operationalization, acceptance criteria, and rollout triggers for cost-saving knobs.
acceptance_criteria: A documented hypothesis template with required fields (motivation, metric delta target, risk, rollback criteria, customer segments)
An experiments registry (spreadsheet + Confluence index) seeded with 12 initial hypotheses covering batching/cache/quant strategies
Automated dashboard showing cost delta, p99 latency, and quality regressions per experiment (refresh < 30m)
Rollout runbook with canary thresholds and automated rollback hooks validated in staging
Prioritized Q2 backlog exported to Linear with owner and estimate for each experiment

2025-03-31: Q2 prioritized backlog locked with Exec review
metrics: Target token-cost reduction: 10% median across seeded experiments
Latency guardrail: < 5% relative increase in p99 for targeted endpoints
Quality guardrail: BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity regression <= 1% as measured by eval prompt set
Operational metric: rollout automation success rate >= 95% (staging)
Signal coverage: at least 80% of experiments produce KPI and regression signals within 24h
work_items: Create experiments registry and Confluence index
Instrument experiment tags and telemetry in runtime (ENG)
Draft rollout runbook and automation scripts (SRE/ENG)
Schedule Exec review for backlog prioritization
risks: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization on tail prompts
Unanticipated latency increases from larger batch windows for low-throughput endpoints
Telemetry gaps leading to false positives/negatives in rollback triggers
Customer sensitive workloads being inadvertently included in experiments
mitigations: Require canary and explicit customer segment exclusions for high-impact experiments
Quality gating with synthetic prompt-set and production shadow evals
Progressive rollout thresholds with automated rollback at each stage
Pre-experiment checklist enforced via PR template and approvals
notes: Trade-offs discussed: pursuit of token-cost reduction versus SLO adherence; we prioritize conservative latency/quality guardrails for customer-facing endpoints
Decision 2025-02-04: Use 12 initial hypotheses to balance breadth and measurement bandwidth
We will prefer configurability (toggles) to binary merges to enable quick rollback
